audit.primary_source_citation: Lee CL, Vijayan M, Wang X, Lam KKW, Koistinen H, Seppälä M, Li RHW, Ng EHY, Yeung WSB, Chiu PCN. "Glycodelin-A stimulates the conversion of human peripheral blood CD16-CD56bright NK cell to a decidual NK cell-like phenotype." Hum Reprod. 2019 Apr 1;34(4):689-701. doi:10.1093/humrep/dey378. PMID 30597092. This is the FIRST and, as of this audit, the ONLY primary paper asserting GdA-driven dNK conversion. Prior GdA/NK primary work from the same Hong Kong group (Lee CL et al., Fertil Steril 2010;94:769-71, PMID 19945098) reported only cytokine modulation (IL-6, IL-13, GM-CSF) with explicitly no effect on viability or cytotoxicity, and made no conversion claim; Bolton et al., Am J Reprod Immunol 1991 (PMID 1840727, PP14/glycodelin suppresses NK activity) is a function-suppression claim, not a lineage claim. So priority for "GdA converts NK toward dNK" rests entirely on Lee 2019.
audit.fulltext_unavailable_reason: Not in PMC/Europe PMC — lit.py returned STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_30597092.txt). Human Reproduction is paywalled. Methods, Results and Limitations were recovered by WebFetch against the publisher HTML (academic.oup.com/humrep/article/34/4/689/5266109) across three targeted passes, which returned verbatim quoted sentences for culture conditions, purity, dose, duration, controls and per-figure N. Marked PARTIAL rather than TRUE because these are model-mediated extractions of the publisher page rather than the raw PDF/XML, and two numbers stayed unrecoverable: the number of women donating first-trimester decidua and the number donating placental tissue for extravillous trophoblast isolation are not stated in the retrievable text.
audit.species: Human (Homo sapiens) only. Peripheral blood from female Hong Kong Red Cross blood donors; first-trimester decidua and placenta from women undergoing surgical termination of pregnancy; HUVEC. No animal work anywhere in the paper.
audit.what_was_measured: In human cells in vitro: peripheral-blood CD16-CD56bright NK cells were negatively immuno-magnetically separated and CD56-microbead-enriched from female Hong Kong Red Cross blood donations (purity >95%), then 1x10^6 cells were cultured 5 days in RPMI-1640 + 10% FBS + 500 IU/mL rhIL-2 + 5 ng/mL rhIL-15, with or without 5 ug/mL glycodelin-A immuno-affinity-purified from human amniotic fluid. At day 5 the readouts were: surface CD9, CD49a, CD151, CD158a and intracellular VEGF by flow cytometry (N=5 donors); secreted angiogenic proteins by cytokine array and VEGF/IGFBP-1 by ELISA (N=3); GdA binding and surface L-selectin/Siglec-7 by flow cytometry on normal vs sialidase-treated GdA (N=4); GdA/L-selectin association by immunoprecipitation; ERK phosphorylation by Western blot; and functional assays on GdA-conditioned NK spent media — HUVEC tube formation and trans-well migration, and trans-well invasion/migration of primary first-trimester extravillous trophoblasts — with anti-VEGF/anti-IGFBP-1 and anti-L-selectin blocking antibodies. Only CD9, CD49a and VEGF rose significantly (P<0.05); CD151 and CD158a did not shift to the dNK pattern. The measurement is day-5 marker and secretome drift in a bulk, cytokine-driven culture — no cell was observed to become another cell.
audit.n: 5 (main flow-cytometry marker experiments); 4 (GdA-binding / L-selectin / Siglec-7 experiments); 3 (angiogenesis cytokine array). Number of decidual-tissue donors and first-trimester placental donors: NOT STATED in the retrievable text.
audit.n_unit: independent human peripheral-blood donors (Hong Kong Red Cross blood donations), NOT cells. Cells per condition were 1x10^6, which is an input quantity, not a replicate count.
audit.controls: (1) Vehicle-equivalent control: "NK cells cultured under the same conditions without GdA were used as the control" — i.e. the control arm still received 500 IU/mL IL-2 + 5 ng/mL IL-15 for 5 days, so the comparison is GdA-on-top-of-strong-cytokine-stimulation, not GdA vs quiescence. (2) Isotype IgG for flow cytometry. (3) De-sialylated GdA (sialidase-agarose treated) as a glycan-dependence control. (4) Anti-L-selectin functional blocking antibody; anti-VEGF and anti-IGFBP-1 blocking antibodies in the HUVEC/trophoblast assays. (5) CD16+CD56dim NK cells as a comparator subset for binding. (6) Primary dNK cells shown alongside treated blood NK in some figures as a phenotypic reference. NOT present: any protein/glycoprotein-load control (e.g. BSA or an irrelevant sialylated glycoprotein at 5 ug/mL), heat-denatured GdA, a cell-number/proliferation readout, CFSE dilution, or a day-0 baseline frequency of CD9+/CD49a+ cells within the CD56bright gate. Viability was addressed only as "GdA treatment at the concentration used did not affect the viability of NK cells as demonstrated by XTT viability assay (data not shown)."
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: SELECTION/EXPANSION OF A PRE-EXISTING SUBSET, which this design cannot exclude. Peripheral-blood CD56bright NK cells are not uniform for CD9 or CD49a; GdA binds via sialylated glycans to L-selectin, which the paper itself shows is expressed on CD56bright but not CD56dim cells, and L-selectin ligation plus 5 days of 500 IU/mL IL-2 and IL-15 is a potent survival/proliferation signal. A GdA-driven survival or proliferative advantage for the CD9+CD49a+ fraction already present at day 0 would produce exactly the observed bulk shift with no cell ever changing identity. Nothing in the methods discriminates the two: no CFSE/CTV dilution, no barcoding, no clonal or single-cell tracking, no absolute cell counts, no day-0 subset frequency, and viability only as unshown XTT data. A second, independent alternative is MARKER ARTEFACT OF PROLIFERATION: CD9 is acquired by ordinary NK cells during cytokine-driven cell-cycle entry — Orrantia et al. (iScience 2022, PMID 36262311) found blood NK cells acquire a "decidual-like" transcriptional profile including CD9 during post-autoHSCT reconstitution dominated by cell-cycle and DNA-replication programmes, and those CD9+ cells carried HIGHER granzyme B and perforin, the opposite of the tolerogenic dNK phenotype. A third: the phenotype is not GdA-specific — hypoxia + TGF-beta1 + 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine (Cerdeira et al., J Immunol 2013, PMID 23487420) and TGF-beta alone (Keskin et al., PNAS 2007, PMID 17360654) already produce CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ "dNK-like" cells, so a 2-of-4-marker shift is a generic culture output rather than evidence of a GdA-instructed lineage decision. The paper's own data undercut conversion: CD151 and CD158a, the other two dNK markers assayed, did NOT convert.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND — searched and read. (1) Orrantia et al., iScience 2022;25:105235 (PMID 36262311 / PMC9574507, full text archived): CD9+ "decidual-like" NK cells expand IN VIVO in human blood after autologous HSCT during a proliferation-dominated reconstitution and express MORE granzyme B and perforin than CD9- NK cells — decoupling CD9/decidual-like gene signature from the non-cytotoxic dNK identity and showing the marker tracks proliferation, not decidualization. (2) Niehrs et al., Nat Immunol 2025 (PMID 41087727 / PMC12571907, archived): human CD56bright NK cells show TRANSIENT tissue residency with lymphatic egress and recirculation, so acquisition of residency-associated markers by CD56bright cells is reversible traffic biology, not a terminal lineage conversion. (3) Vacca et al., PNAS 2011;108:2402-7 (PMID 21248224): CD34+ haematopoietic precursors resident in human decidua differentiate into NK cells on contact with decidual stromal cells — an origin for dNK that requires no blood-NK conversion at all. (4) Sojka et al., eLife 2014 (PMC3975579): tissue-resident uterine NK/ILC1 are a lineage distinct from conventional circulating NK cells — the two-independent-origins alternative. (5) Priority/specificity counter-evidence: Keskin 2007 (PNAS, TGF-beta) and Cerdeira 2013 (J Immunol, hypoxia+TGF-beta1+decitabine) obtained the same CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ readout from unrelated stimuli. NOT FOUND despite searching: any direct replication of the GdA-specific result by an independent laboratory, and any experiment (of any kind) testing GdA-driven dNK conversion in vivo.
audit.downstream_dependency: Concrete named dependencies: (1) Lee CL, Guo Y, ... Chiu PCN, "Decidual glycodelin-A polarizes human monocytes into a decidual macrophage-like phenotype through Siglec-7," J Cell Sci 2020;133:jcs244400 — the same group's direct follow-on, which generalizes T5 into a framework of GdA as the master decidualizing signal for maternal leukocytes; if the NK conversion is really subset selection, the parallel monocyte "polarization" claim inherits the identical confound. (2) Chiu group review, "The functional roles of protein glycosylation in human maternal-fetal crosstalk," Hum Reprod Update 2024 — presents GdA-driven dNK conversion as established mechanism in a high-impact review that sets field consensus. (3) "Dual Role of Natural Killer Cells in Early Pregnancy: ... Therapeutic Potential in Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion and Recurrent Implantation Failure," Cell Prolif 2025 (PMID 40325291) — cites T5 to support therapeutic re-education of peripheral NK toward a dNK phenotype in RSA/RIF, i.e. a clinical-intervention rationale resting on the conversion premise. Rated MEDIUM not HIGH because 44 citing works are overwhelmingly reviews rather than experiments built on top of it, no independent lab has replicated it, and the mechanistic core of the pregnancy field (dNK origin) rests on Vacca 2011, Vento-Tormo 2018 and mouse tissue-resident-NK work rather than on GdA.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The IN VITRO call is CONFIRMED, not overturned: Lee 2019 contains no animal or in vivo experiment of any kind, and this is structural rather than an oversight — PAEP/glycodelin has no mouse or rat ortholog (the gene is lost in mouse, rat, rabbit, tarsier, megabat and dolphin, and is functional in higher primates), so the conventional rodent test of this claim does not exist and cannot be run. What the audit DOES overturn is the verb in the claim. "Converts" is not supported at the level the word implies. The measurement is a day-5 bulk-population shift in 2 of 4 assayed dNK markers (CD9, CD49a up; CD151 and CD158a NOT converted) plus VEGF, in n=5 blood donors, in cells simultaneously receiving 500 IU/mL IL-2 and 5 ng/mL IL-15, against a no-GdA arm that received the same cytokines. There is no clonal or single-cell tracking, no CFSE, no cell counts, no day-0 subset frequency, and viability appears only as unshown XTT data — so selective survival/expansion of a pre-existing CD9+CD49a+ fraction within the CD56bright gate is fully consistent with every reported result. The strongest classification the methods support is INF_INVITRO with INF_MARKER; nothing in the paper reaches any OBS_ class. The authors themselves concede "a major limitation of this study is that the trophoblast and the NK cells in the co-culture experiments are not isolated from the same donor and there was a small sample size" and state in the abstract that "these results need to be confirmed with human primary dNK cells." The claim should be restated as: GdA, added to IL-2/IL-15-stimulated human blood CD56bright NK cells for 5 days in vitro, increases CD9, CD49a and VEGF via sialic-acid-dependent L-selectin binding and ERK activation, in 5 donors, with lineage conversion untested.
audit.methods_quote: "NK cells (1 x 10^6) were cultured in the Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI-1640) medium supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (FBS), 500 IU/mL of recombinant human interleukin (IL)-2 (Peprotech), 5 ng/mL of recombinant human IL-15 (Peprotech) and 5 ug/mL of GdA for 5 days." / "NK cells cultured under the same conditions without GdA were used as the control." / "The purity of the isolated CD16-CD56bright NK cell was >95%." / "GdA treatment at the concentration used did not affect the viability of NK cells as demonstrated by XTT viability assay (data not shown)." / Limitations: "A major limitation of this study is that the trophoblast and the NK cells in the co-culture experiments are not isolated from the same donor and there was a small sample size."
audit.notes: HINT VERIFICATION: the "Lee/Chiu et al." hint is CORRECT — Lee Cheuk-Lun is first author and Philip C.N. Chiu is senior author (University of Hong Kong / HKU-Shenzhen), PMID 30597092. Dose 5 ug/mL, duration 5 days, n=5 donors, markers CD9/CD49a/CD151/CD158a/VEGF, all confirmed against the publisher's Methods and Results. NO in vivo work exists on this claim — searched and not found — and this is structurally so, since PAEP is absent from the mouse and rat genomes; the only in vivo experiment anywhere adjacent is Cavalli et al., PLoS One 2016 (PMID 27736914, archived), which transferred hypoxia/TGF-beta1/decitabine-induced dNK-like cells into mice and improved utero-placental perfusion — that is OBS_TRANSFER for a DIFFERENT induction protocol, not for GdA, and cannot be borrowed to support T5. IMPORTANT ASYMMETRY: the paper's own binding data are the tidiest result (GdA binds CD56bright > CD56dim, sialidase-sensitive, L-selectin-dependent, ERK-dependent) and those conclusions are well controlled; it is specifically the LINEAGE claim that outruns the methods. The 2-of-4 marker failure (CD151, CD158a unchanged) is reported by the authors and is the single most useful internal check against the conversion framing. adv.challenge_reason: I re-pulled the primary source myself. `lit.py methods 30597092 --tag T5` returns STATUS=ABSTRACT_ONLY (no PMC deposit; archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_30597092.txt), so I independently re-extracted Methods/Results from the publisher HTML (academic.oup.com/humrep/article/34/4/689/5266109). The auditor's methods_quote reproduces VERBATIM and I confirm every load-bearing element: negative immunomagnetic NK isolation + CD56 MicroBeads (or FACS), purity >95%; "NK cells (1 x 10^6) were cultured in the Roswell Park Memorial Institute (RPMI-1640) medium supplemented with 10% foetal bovine serum (FBS), 500 IU/mL of recombinant human interleukin (IL)-2 (Peprotech), 5 ng/mL of recombinant human IL-15 (Peprotech) and 5 ug/mL of GdA for 5 days"; "NK cells cultured under the same conditions without GdA were used as the control"; viability only as "XTT viability assay (data not shown)". CLASSIFICATION UPHELD at INF_INVITRO (with INF_MARKER). The auditor credited NO OBS_* class, and none is owed: there is no live imaging, no barcoding, no genetic lineage tracing, no congenic/adoptive transfer, no knockout. The anti-L-selectin, anti-VEGF and anti-IGFBP-1 blocking antibodies are pharmacological receptor/ligand blockade of a BINDING and SECRETION readout, not a genetic ablation in which "B fails to appear", so they do not reach OBS_GENETIC; and the entity "B" is defined by nothing but surface markers, so even a genetic result would have been marker-defined. I also checked the converse (missed fate-mapping deserving UPGRADE): there is none anywhere in the paper — no animal appears, and I confirm this is structural, since PAEP/glycodelin is primate-restricted, independently corroborated by Dixit/Balakrishnan/Karande, Clin Exp Immunol 2018 (PMID 29271477): "Because glycodelin is found only in certain primates, the hypothesis was investigated in an allograft nude mouse model." So UPHELD, not UPGRADE, not DOWNGRADE. THREE CORRECTIONS the auditor got wrong inside an otherwise sound row. (1) G5 VIOLATION on n_unit: the auditor states n_unit = "independent human peripheral-blood donors (Hong Kong Red Cross blood donations)". The paper's Statistical Analysis section defines N as "the number of NK cell samples" — it does NOT say donors. The auditor silently upgraded an ambiguous unit ("samples") into the strongest reading ("independent donors"). Samples could be repeated preparations or pooled buffy coats; nothing in the retrievable text excludes that. Correct entry: n_unit = independent NK-cell samples, donor-independence NOT STATED. (2) n mis-assignment: the auditor puts the ELISA at N=3. The publisher text gives Fig 2A antibody array N=3 and Fig 2B ELISA N=5; N=3 applies to the antibody array and the Fig 5E immunoprecipitation. Fig 1 (the CD9/CD49a/VEGF marker result that IS the claim) is N=5; Fig 5A-B/5D and Fig 7 are N=4-5. (3) Two additional unshown-data controls the auditor missed, both reported only as "(data not shown)": HUVEC proliferation (Cyquant NF) and JEG-3 proliferation. Combined with the unshown XTT, three separate proliferation/viability controls in this paper exist only as unshown data — which is precisely the axis on which the selection-vs-conversion question turns. WHY INF_INVITRO IS AT THE ABSOLUTE FLOOR OF ITS CLASS: the outcome variable is itself marker similarity (3 readouts moved: CD9, CD49a, VEGF; 2 of the 4 assayed surface dNK markers, CD151 and CD158a, did NOT move), the control arm received the same 500 IU/mL IL-2 + 5 ng/mL IL-15, and there is no CFSE/CTV, no absolute cell count, no day-0 within-gate frequency of CD9+/CD49a+ cells, and no clonal or single-cell tracking. The verb "converts" in the claim is not supported; "shifts the bulk day-5 mean of 3 of 5 assayed readouts" is.
adv.revised_evidence_type_strongest: INF_INVITRO (unchanged). Full set present: INF_INVITRO + INF_MARKER. Not present: OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER, OBS_GENETIC, INF_TRAJECTORY, INF_KINETIC (single day-5 endpoint, no time course, so not even INF_KINETIC is earned).
adv.new_counter_evidence: THREE items the auditor missed, one of which is decisive, plus an internal contradiction in the auditor's own list. (1) DECISIVE MISS — Dixit A & Karande AA, "Glycodelin regulates the numbers and function of peripheral natural killer cells," J Reprod Immunol 2020;137:102625, PMID 31730930 (Indian Institute of Science; archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_31730930.txt). This is the ONLY independent-laboratory primary study of glycodelin acting on human peripheral NK cells, published within a year of Lee 2019, and it is not in the auditor's row at all. It reports that glycodelin "suppresses the cytotoxicity of peripheral NK cells via downregulating perforin, granzyme B and IFNgamma" and — the load-bearing sentence — "Glycodelin also induces caspase-dependent death in ONLY ACTIVATED peripheral NK cells," mediated by CD7, not L-selectin. Selective killing of the activated, cytotoxic, perforin/granzyme-high fraction is a concrete, published, independently-observed MECHANISM that would generate Lee 2019's exact bulk marker shift with no cell ever changing identity: kill the cytotoxic CD9-negative cells and the surviving mean drifts toward CD9+CD49a+VEGF+. This converts the "pre-existing subset was selected, not converted" alternative from a generic design criticism into a specific mechanism demonstrated for this very ligand on this very cell type — and Lee 2019's only rebuttal is an XTT assay shown as "data not shown". It also creates a receptor conflict (Karande: CD7; Lee: L-selectin) for the same ligand on the same cell. The Karande group had already reported GdA-induced NK apoptosis in PMID 29271477 (2018), i.e. BEFORE Lee 2019. (2) MAJOR MISS on marker specificity AND on pre-existence — Gallazzi M, ..., Albini A, Noonan DM, Bruno A, "Prostate Cancer Peripheral Blood NK Cells Show Enhanced CD9, CD49a, CXCR4, CXCL8, MMP-9 Production...," Front Immunol 2020;11:586126, PMID 33569050 / PMC7868409 (OA full text archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_PMC7868409.txt), with its predecessor Bruno et al., FASEB J 2018, PMID 29763380 ("proangiogenic, decidual NK-like cells from patients with colorectal cancer" — note: PRE-dates Lee 2019). Verbatim from the full text: "PCa pTA-NKs acquire the CD56bright CD9+ CD49a+ CXCR4+ phenotype", measured DIRECTLY EX VIVO by flow cytometry on PBMC from prostate cancer patients — men, no pregnancy, no decidua, no glycodelin, no culture — with elevated VEGF mRNA. This establishes that CD9+CD49a+VEGF+ "dNK-like" NK cells PRE-EXIST in human peripheral blood and vary in frequency with host state, which is exactly the pre-existing pool the selection alternative requires and which Lee 2019 never quantifies at day 0. The same paper then shows the readout is stimulus-nonspecific three ways over: TGF-beta at 10 ng/mL for 72 h raised CD56 (p<=0.01), CD9 (p<=0.01) and CD49a (p<=0.05) on healthy-donor blood NK; conditioned media from three unrelated prostate cancer lines (PC-3, DU-145, LNCaP) for 72 h likewise raised CD9, CD49a and CXCR4; and IL-6 did not. So four mechanistically unrelated inputs (GdA, TGF-beta, tumour secretome, and per Cerdeira 2013 hypoxia+TGF-beta1+decitabine) converge on the same 2-marker readout. This is a generic pro-angiogenic/exhausted NK polarization state, not a GdA-instructed decidual lineage decision. The auditor cited Orrantia 2022, Keskin 2007 and Cerdeira 2013 for a weaker version of this point and missed the cancer-blood literature entirely. (3) MISS that cuts BOTH ways, and exposes an internal contradiction in the auditor's row — Tatematsu BK & Sojka DK, "Tissue-resident natural killer cells derived from conventional natural killer cells are regulated by progesterone in the uterus," Mucosal Immunol 2025;18:390-401, PMID 39708955 (archived /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_39708955.txt). Mouse, IN VIVO, parabiosis + intravascular fluorescent antibody labeling + ovariectomy + hormone add-back + progesterone-receptor antagonist: "Our parabiosis studies confirmed that the progesterone-responsive trNK cells are derived from peripheral cNK cells," and "mice OVX at three weeks of age and analyzed as adults lacked uterine trNK cells unless progesterone was administered." Three consequences. (a) It REHABILITATES the general premise the auditor tried to attack — blood cNK really can give rise to uterine tissue-resident NK — so the auditor's blanket "two independent origins" framing is too strong. (b) It supplies a COMPETING, far better-evidenced sufficient driver: progesterone, tested by parabiosis and by receptor antagonist, in vivo. GdA is not needed to explain uterine NK residency. (c) Critically, it is by DOROTHY SOJKA, the senior author of the very eLife 2014 paper (PMID 24714492) the auditor cited as counter-evidence #4 for "two independent origins". The auditor cited an 11-year-old paper as establishing a distinct-lineage claim that the same laboratory has since qualified for the uterine, progesterone-responsive compartment. Citing Sojka 2014 without Sojka 2025 is a stale-citation error. Note also the 2025 abstract's own verb: "medroxyprogesterone 17-acetate-induced EXPANSION of cNK-derived trNK cells" — expansion, i.e. the very axis Lee 2019 does not measure. SEARCHED AND CONFIRMED ABSENT (G3-clean): I enumerated all 44 Europe PMC citing works of MED/30597092 and read the title of every one. There is NO independent replication of the GdA-driven dNK conversion result. The only citing primary papers in the same space are the same group's own follow-on (J Cell Sci 2020, PMID 32513821), and unrelated-stimulus in vitro "transformation" papers of the same weak design (Int J Mol Sci 2025, PMID 40332223, "JEG-3 Trophoblast Cells Influence ILC-like Transformation of NK Cells In Vitro"; Immunobiology 2021, PMID 34365089, which uses the NK-92 leukaemia CELL LINE, where a phenotype shift in a clonal line cannot even in principle speak to subset selection). I also ran two PubMed searches for a transcriptome-level comparison of in vitro-converted dNK-like cells against bona fide dNK, and for a human recruitment-vs-local-proliferation (Ki67) study of dNK origin: both returned ZERO hits — searched, NONE found.
adv.crossfield_g4_findings: The mechanism T5 invokes is generic: a circulating lymphocyte acquires a tissue-residency/tolerogenic program under a locally secreted factor. The TRM, ILC and myeloid fields have each already run this exact question with assays Lee 2019 does not use, and all three converge on the same verdict: a bulk marker shift in culture is not evidence of conversion, and every time the question was settled properly the answer changed. (A) TRM — WHAT THE FIELD REQUIRED AS PROOF. Mackay LK et al., Nat Immunol 2013, PMID 24162776, "The developmental pathway for CD103+CD8+ tissue-resident memory T cells of skin": the field did NOT accept TGF-beta-induced CD103 in a dish as demonstrating that circulating cells become resident. It required transfer of congenically/TCR-marked cells into recipients with in vivo tracking of the SAME marked cells — an OBS_TRANSFER design. Zhang N & Bevan MJ, Immunity 2013, PMID 24076049, "Transforming growth factor-beta signaling controls the formation and maintenance of gut-resident memory T cells by regulating migration and retention": conditional deletion of the TGF-beta receptor in T cells so that TRM fail to form — an OBS_GENETIC design. That is the evidentiary bar for "factor X converts A into tissue-resident B", and note that both papers concern TGF-beta, the very cytokine that Gallazzi 2020 (PMID 33569050) shows reproduces GdA's entire CD9/CD49a readout. The TRM field cleared this bar in 2013; T5 has not cleared it in 2026. (B) TRM — THE MARKER ITSELF IS AN ACTIVATION MARKER. Shiow LR et al., Nature 2006, PMID 16525420, "CD69 acts downstream of interferon-alpha/beta to inhibit S1P1 and lymphocyte egress from lymphoid organs": the canonical residency marker CD69 is an activation-induced protein, so any activating culture manufactures "residency" phenotype by construction. This is the single most transferable lesson to T5. Lee 2019 cultured for 5 days in 500 IU/mL IL-2 plus 5 ng/mL IL-15 — a maximally activating condition — and scored CD49a (ITGA1, an activation-inducible adhesion integrin) and CD9 (a tetraspanin induced on cycling/activated lymphocytes). Because the GdA arm and the control arm both received the cytokines, the paper controls for the cytokines' MEAN effect but not for a GdA x activation interaction, and not at all for differential survival across the pre-existing activation states within the gate — which is exactly what Karande's PMID 31730930 says GdA does (kills ONLY activated NK cells). (C) TRM — THE FIELD HAD TO INVENT A CONTROL TO SEPARATE "IS IN THE TISSUE" FROM "IS OF THE TISSUE". Anderson KG et al., Nat Protoc 2014, PMID 24385150, intravascular staining: a large fraction of lymphocytes recovered by tissue digestion and called resident were in fact still vascular. Structural analogue for T5: the field learned that you cannot infer a cell's identity from the compartment-level readout without a control that separates the two populations. Lee 2019 has no control separating "a CD56bright cell became CD9+CD49a+" from "a CD9+CD49a+ CD56bright cell was already there and outlived its neighbours." (D) ILC — PARABIOSIS IS THE ARBITER, AND IT HAS ALREADY BEEN RUN ON THIS EXACT TISSUE. Gasteiger G, Fan X, Dikiy S, Lee SY, Rudensky AY, Science 2015, PMID 26472762, "Tissue residency of innate lymphoid cells in lymphoid and nonlymphoid organs": parabiosis established that ILCs in nonlymphoid organs are largely tissue-resident and are NOT replenished from the circulation at steady state, placing the burden of proof on anyone claiming blood-to-tissue conversion. Then Tatematsu & Sojka, Mucosal Immunol 2025, PMID 39708955, ran parabiosis plus intravascular labeling plus ovariectomy plus PR antagonist on the UTERUS specifically and found uterine trNK ARE cNK-derived and progesterone-driven. So for the precise biological question behind T5, an OBS_DIRECT-grade in vivo answer already exists in mouse — and it names progesterone, not glycodelin, as the driver. Glycodelin cannot be tested this way at all (PAEP is primate-restricted; PMID 29271477). The correct reading is therefore not "conversion is impossible" but "conversion is real, has been demonstrated by parabiosis with a different and better-evidenced driver, and GdA's specific contribution remains untested by any assay capable of detecting it." (E) MYELOID — THE CANONICAL CAUTIONARY TALE, AND IT IS AN EXACT STRUCTURAL MATCH. "Blood monocytes convert into tissue macrophages" was textbook for decades on the strength of marker similarity and in vitro differentiation — the same two evidence classes as T5. It was overturned by fate mapping: Ginhoux F et al., Science 2010, PMID 20966214, showed adult microglia derive from yolk-sac primitive macrophages, not blood monocytes; Hashimoto D et al., Immunity 2013, PMID 23601688, showed by parabiosis and fate mapping that tissue-resident macrophages self-maintain locally with minimal monocyte input. The specific error in the old literature was reading a bulk phenotype shift as conversion when the real driver was LOCAL PROLIFERATION of a pre-existing resident population — numerically identical to the confound in T5, and the reason CFSE/CTV, absolute counts and day-0 frequencies are non-optional. (F) MYELOID — CULTURE IS THE WRONG PLACE TO DEMONSTRATE ACQUISITION OF A TISSUE IDENTITY. Lavin Y et al., Cell 2014, PMID 25480296, and Gosselin D et al., Cell 2014, PMID 25480297, showed the tissue environment writes the macrophage enhancer landscape and that removing macrophages from tissue into culture rapidly erases the tissue-specific program. If a genuine tissue identity is continuously imposed by the environment and is lost within days ex vivo, then a 5-day dish containing one purified protein is close to the least capable system for demonstrating that a cell has ACQUIRED that identity — the assay is running against the biology. This is a general methodological verdict from an adjacent field that applies directly and was not considered in the row under review. NET G4 VERDICT: the cross-field literature does not overturn the possibility of blood-NK-to-uterine-NK conversion — Tatematsu/Sojka 2025 supports it — but it comprehensively overturns the SUFFICIENCY of Lee 2019's evidence for it, identifies the precise uncontrolled confounds (activation-induced markers, proliferation, differential survival), names the assays that would settle it (congenic/adoptive transfer, parabiosis, barcoding, CFSE, conditional receptor deletion), and supplies a better-evidenced competing driver (progesterone).

adv.load_bearing_reason: DOWNGRADE MEDIUM -> LOW. The auditor's own stated grounds for MEDIUM are the definition of LOW: they wrote that the 44 citing works "are overwhelmingly reviews rather than experiments built on top of it", that "no independent lab has replicated it", and that the field's mechanistic core "rests on Vacca 2011, Vento-Tormo 2018 and mouse tissue-resident-NK work rather than on GdA." Having enumerated and title-read all 44 Europe PMC citing works myself, I confirm every one of those observations and add the decisive one the auditor did not make: the ONE independent laboratory that ran a primary experiment on glycodelin x peripheral NK cells built in the OPPOSITE direction. Dixit & Karande, J Reprod Immunol 2020, PMID 31730930, report GdA suppressing cytotoxicity and inducing caspase-dependent death in activated NK cells via CD7 — not conversion, and via a different receptor than Lee's L-selectin. A claim that the only independent group to touch it implicitly declined to adopt is not bearing load; it is being routed around. CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCIES (all PMID-verified), and why each survives T5's falsification, which is what forces LOW: (1) Lee CL, ..., Chiu PCN, "Decidual glycodelin-A polarizes human monocytes into a decidual macrophage-like phenotype through Siglec-7," J Cell Sci 2020;133:jcs244400, PMID 32513821 — the same group's direct follow-on and the strongest genuine dependency, since it generalizes T5 into a framework of GdA as the master decidualizing signal for maternal leukocytes and inherits the identical uncontrolled confound (bulk marker drift in cytokine-supported culture with no proliferation or differential-survival control). But it is a self-citation and a separate experiment on a different cell type: if T5's NK conversion is subset selection, the monocyte paper is weakened by analogy, not logically falsified. (2) Chiu group review, "The functional roles of protein glycosylation in human maternal-fetal crosstalk," Hum Reprod Update 2024, PMID 37699855 — presents GdA-driven dNK conversion as established mechanism in a top-tier review that sets field consensus; falsifying T5 costs a paragraph, not a research programme. (3) "Dual Role of Natural Killer Cells in Early Pregnancy: Immunopathological Implications and Therapeutic Potential in Recurrent Spontaneous Abortion and Recurrent Implantation Failure," Cell Prolif 2025, PMID 40325291 — cites T5 to support therapeutic re-education of peripheral NK toward a dNK phenotype in RSA/RIF. This is the only place T5 touches a clinical rationale, and it is the reason load-bearing is not ZERO; but that rationale rests primarily on Keskin 2007 (PMID 17360654) and Cerdeira 2013 (PMID 23487420), which established the general in vitro conversion phenomenon years earlier with unrelated stimuli, so it survives T5's removal intact. (4) The two citing primary papers nearest in kind — Int J Mol Sci 2025, PMID 40332223 ("JEG-3 Trophoblast Cells Influence ILC-like Transformation of NK Cells In Vitro") and Immunobiology 2021, PMID 34365089 (NK-92 cell line phenotype shift) — cite T5 as precedent for a design, not as a premise they depend on. DECIDING TEST: if T5 were retracted tomorrow, no experimental programme would collapse. The field's account of dNK origin would be untouched, because it is carried by Vento-Tormo 2018 (PMID 30429548), Strunz 2021 (PMID 33617461), Vacca 2011 and now Tatematsu & Sojka 2025 (PMID 39708955), whose parabiosis result attributes uterine trNK derivation to progesterone and needs no glycodelin at all. That is LOW.
adv.better_primary_source: NO BETTER PRIMARY SOURCE EXISTS — the auditor's identification of Lee CL, Vijayan M, Wang X, Lam KKW, Koistinen H, Seppala M, Li RHW, Ng EHY, Yeung WSB, Chiu PCN, Hum Reprod 2019;34(4):689-701, doi:10.1093/humrep/dey378, PMID 30597092 is CORRECT and I independently verified priority rather than accepting it. I retrieved the complete PubMed corpus of glycodelin/PAEP/PP14 x natural killer papers (22 records) and read the year/journal/title of every one. Pre-2019 there are exactly three primary NK-relevant entries and none makes a lineage claim: Bolton et al., Am J Reprod Immunol 1991, PMID 1840727 ("Suppression by human placental protein 14 of natural killer cell activity") is function suppression; Lee CL et al., Fertil Steril 2010, PMID 19945098 ("Glycodelin-A modulates cytokine production of peripheral blood natural killer cells") is cytokine modulation only; and Dixit, Balakrishnan & Karande, Clin Exp Immunol 2018, PMID 29271477 reports GdA-induced apoptosis in activated NK cells — the opposite of conversion. Nothing pre-2019 asserts GdA-driven dNK conversion, so priority for T5 rests entirely on Lee 2019, exactly as the auditor stated. TWO REFINEMENTS THE AUDITOR SHOULD HAVE MADE. (a) PRIORITY IS NARROWER THAN THE ROW IMPLIES. Lee 2019 is NOT the first source for the underlying phenomenon "human peripheral blood NK cells can be pushed toward a dNK-like phenotype in vitro" — that belongs to Keskin DB et al., PNAS 2007, PMID 17360654 (TGF-beta converts CD16+ blood NK toward CD16- dNK-like), extended by Cerdeira AS et al., J Immunol 2013, PMID 23487420 (hypoxia + TGF-beta1 + 5-aza-2'-deoxycytidine). Lee 2019's only novel element is substituting GdA as the driver; the assay, the readout and the conclusion structure were already in place. The row should record Lee 2019 as first source for the GdA-SPECIFIC claim and Keskin 2007 as first source for the general phenomenon, because that is what determines how much of T5 is actually at risk. (b) FULLTEXT STATUS: PARTIAL is the right call and I reproduced it independently. lit.py returns ABSTRACT_ONLY (no PMC deposit; /home/user/aaa/refs/T5_30597092.txt is an abstract stub) and Human Reproduction is paywalled; I recovered Methods, Results and Limitations by WebFetch against academic.oup.com/humrep/article/34/4/689/5266109 and every one of the auditor's quoted sentences matched verbatim.
